about: Born, Not Made, tail copy variant, round 2 (23 Nov 2026). Frame: x along the tank toward the head's mouth at the start, y port, z up, metres; z = 0 the inner floor of the bodies, the tank floor glass at -3 mm.

tank.name: made to order (estimate): 2.72 x 0.86 m outside, 2.69 x 0.83 m inside

stages.name: Print the new tail
stages.text: The needle prints the new tail whole, in one print, folded flat on the bowl floor: laid flat, Z folded 3 across and 3 along, 18 layers, 152 x 192 x 79 mm, two skins and the webs between them in Dragon Skin 30.

stages.name: Cure
stages.text: Dragon Skin 30 cures in the gel for 16 hours (Smooth-On bulletin). Tool change in the tail: print needle off, holder on.

stages.name: Birth: the folds open
stages.text: The ball needle of the holder in the valve at the rim. The keel fills first and opens the first lengthwise folds, paying the strip out from the front while the rim stays at the back of the pack; the nose goes up the chin of the head and onto the lower lip, cupped.

stages.name: Birth: push while inflating
stages.text: The holder, then its folding crank, pushes the rim at 2 mm/s; air is fed with the advance, so each section opens only outside: across first, then the quilt. Inside and on the lip the strip stays flat and cupped. The rim goes 186 mm, the last lengthwise folds open as it goes, and the nose comes down onto the tank floor.

stages.name: Birth: the parent backs away
stages.text: The needle leaves the valve. The parent backs 317 mm on the wheels of its tail, its head with it; the nose of the new tail rests on the tank floor, so the rest slides over the lip, fills outside and settles on the floor.

stages.name: The parent and its head move aside
stages.text: The parent backs its head away from the new tail and toward the port glass on the wheels of its tail, the head dragged on the floor (as the relay of the quilted head simulator).

stages.name: Tilt release
stages.text: A cord tilts the nine magnets of the tail face on their hinged tabs; they peel off the steel disks of the head's cuff. The tail backs 35 mm. The old head stays at the port glass with its gel.

stages.name: Round the old head
stages.text: The tail backs 175 mm, shunts once to starboard (forward 175 mm, back 175 mm), turns into the starboard lane, drives past the old head and comes onto the centre line in front of the new tail. Nothing is between them now: the head that bore the new tail stands aside.

stages.name: Base: from the tray
stages.text: It turns to the tray. The base stands in its floor bay on its drive frame, in its sealed shroud. The magnet lands on the steel pad of the grip boss on the turret, the ball needle enters the socket 28 mm ahead: the magnet holds, the needle keeps the base from turning. The base is lifted 12 mm, no more: at this depth the water carries most of it.

stages.name: Base: carried to the plate
stages.text: It backs out, turns on its wheels and drives to the assembly plate beside the new tail, the base held low in front of its face.

stages.name: Base: set down
stages.text: The parent stands beside the assembly plate, a steel cast plate on the glass beside the new tail's face. It sets the base down on the plate: the two wheels of the frame drop into the plate's slots. Magnet off; the needle leaves the socket.

stages.name: Power pack: from the tray
stages.text: The power pack (three 18650 cells in series in a sealed sleeve) stands in its cradle. Magnet on the pad, needle in the socket, lifted out of the cradle.

stages.name: Power pack: carried to the plate
stages.text: It backs out, turns on its wheels and drives to the assembly plate beside the new tail, the power pack held low in front of its face.

stages.name: Power pack: set down
stages.text: The pack goes on the bracket at the front of the drive frame; its pads meet the pogo pins of the frame. The new arm has power.

stages.name: Upper arm: from the tray
stages.text: The upper arm with the elbow block lies in its cradle in the attitude it will go on. Magnet on the pad of its boss, needle in the socket; lifted clear of the cradle walls.

stages.name: Upper arm: carried to the plate
stages.text: It backs out, turns on its wheels and drives to the assembly plate beside the new tail, the upper arm held low in front of its face.

stages.name: Upper arm: set down
stages.text: The new arm holds its shoulder where the parent can reach. The upper arm goes down onto the shoulder pins and the latch clicks. Magnet off.

stages.name: Forearm: from the tray
stages.text: The forearm in its cradle, in the attitude it will go on. Magnet on the pad of its boss, needle in the socket; lifted.

stages.name: Forearm: carried to the plate
stages.text: It backs out, turns on its wheels and drives to the assembly plate beside the new tail, the forearm held low in front of its face.

stages.name: Forearm: set down
stages.text: The new arm holds its upper arm out. The forearm goes down onto the elbow and clicks. Magnet off.

stages.name: End effector: from the tray
stages.text: The end effector with its rotary flange. Magnet on the pad, needle in the socket; lifted.

stages.name: End effector: carried to the plate
stages.text: It backs out, turns on its wheels and drives to the assembly plate beside the new tail, the end effector held low in front of its face.

stages.name: End effector: set down
stages.text: The end effector goes down onto the wrist and clicks. The new arm is whole.

stages.name: The new arm folds
stages.text: The new arm is whole. Powered by its own pack it folds up; the parent backs away to give it room.

stages.name: It drives into the new tail
stages.text: On the two N20 wheels of its frame the new arm backs round and into the new tail through its open face: the wheels run in two slots of its floor down to the glass, and the frame's four pins click into the cast sockets of the floor where the base of a tail stands.

stages.name: Face to face
stages.text: The parent docks face to face with the new tail: the nine magnets of its face on the steel disks of the new tail's face cuff, as a tail docks to a head.

stages.name: Gel ballast
stages.text: Docked, the parent pumps gel from the bottle outside the tank through its line into the new tail's circuits in place of their air (a relief valve lets the air out), at 0.1 L a minute: the body becomes heavy above the water line and holds down the frame of the new arm, pinned into its floor. Gel is the only ballast of a new body; no steel.

stages.name: Its own arm
stages.text: The tilt release lets go and the parent backs 300 mm away. The new tail has a body, an arm, power and gel ballast; it has no tool and no sensors yet.

stages.name: The new tail turns to the tray
stages.text: On the wheels of its drive frame, powered from its pack, the new tail turns on the spot and drives to the tray.

stages.name: It takes a holder
stages.text: Tool change, as the parent does it in its own tail: the bare quick release of the new arm comes down onto the holder standing in its saddle on the tray and clicks; the holder lifts out of the saddle. The new arm now has an electromagnet, a ball needle and a crank.

stages.name: It puts a tile set into its own wall
stages.text: Magnet on the steel disk of the tile set, the ball needle into the well of its cradle. The arm draws the tile into its own body over the pack and lays it on the lower skin of the pocket on the port flank, then slides it 16 mm in under the two lips of the pocket, the needle running in the slot of the lower skin. Magnet off; the magnet lifts out between the lips. A Core tile, two Sense tiles (motion, pressure), a Power tile and an mp6 pump, on one cast tile (after bergsonne.io/tiles and the quilted head kit).

stages.name: Two tails
stages.text: The new tail backs away from the tray: one body born from the head, an arm the parent put together for it, power, gel ballast, a tool and a first set of sensors it took itself. The parent waits beside its old head.

checks.name: The parent's tail is a quilted double wall from the first frame, built as the head is built: two skins joined by webs along the body, 72 channels round it, the outer skin an arc of 55 degrees between two webs, the inner one of 25, the floor a flat double skin of 2.5 mm; cross seams at the thirds of the body, staggered. The inner skin follows the outer surface of the doublewall tail, so the arm, the tools and the store keep their places

checks.name: The new tail is one body, printed whole: the parent's tail copied, the same construction and the same outline, nose to face cuff
checks.value: 0.547 m2 outer, 0.478 m2 inner, 1.34 L of Dragon Skin 30

checks.name: The whole tail folds as the head does (laid flat, Z folded 3 across and 3 along, 18 layers of 4.4 mm): 152 x 192 x 79.2 mm. It is 9 mm longer than the head's own pack (143 x 194 x 79 mm), not taller: it lies on the flat floor of the bowl from 114 to 266 mm (the floor is flat from 32 to 268 mm). Folding 4 along to keep 143 mm would give 24 layers, 106 mm, over the 83.2 mm under the needle

No part needs deep water here: the base, sealed, nearly floats at this depth and is lifted only 8 mm; the other parts weigh less than the payload in air

Its links reach out with up to 1.30 N m, so the frame is pinned into four cast sockets printed into the new tail's floor and the body holds it down: with its circuits filled with gel (2.03 L above the water line, 20.0 N) the body gives 2.52 N m at a lever of 100 mm

checks.name: Every pick and every set down is a sequence: the holder comes over the part from a reachable direction, the magnet lands on the steel pad of the part's grip boss and the ball needle enters its socket 28 mm ahead (15 mm deep), magnet on, a straight vertical lift out of the cradle, a carry pose clear of the parent's gel face, the turn, the drive to its stand beside the assembly plate, a vertical descent onto the plate or joint, magnet off, a vertical lift. Moves between holds run in joint space inside the DexArm's ranges

notes: The parent's tail is no longer a hard shell: it is a quilted double wall from the first frame, built like the head, with its inner skin where the shell's outer surface was. The DexArm stands on a printed seat plate on the floor skin; the store hangs on a printed rack on the same plate; two N20 wheels in slots of the floor skin drive it; 1.2 kg of steel on the plate (allowed for the parent, as in the quilted head simulator) gives the wheels their grip.

The water stays at the level of the quilted head simulator (80.7 mm). The earlier round raised it to 270 mm so the parent could lift the base; here the base, in its sealed shroud, nearly floats at this depth and is lifted only 8 mm, so the head stays on the floor and the tails keep their wheels on the glass.

The new tail is printed whole, in one print, and born once: nose first over the lower lip, so that it comes to rest in front of the head with its open face toward it. The earlier round printed it in two halves; the whole tail fits the bowl folded 3 x 3 as the head does, 9 mm longer than the head's own pack and no taller.

The new arm is put together on an assembly plate on the glass beside the new tail's face, not inside it: docked face to face, the parent's holder could not reach the join poses over its floor without touching its walls. For each part the parent stands beside the plate at a place the script searched (the pad in reach from above, its arm and tool clear of its own wall on the way in and out). Five trips. Then the new arm drives itself into the new tail on its own wheels.
The holder's heading is its base angle (no wrist): the parts stand on the tray turned so they arrive at their seats at the right heading.

Each part carries a grip boss: a printed block with a 20 x 3 mm steel pad and a 3.2 mm socket 28 mm from it, placed by the script where the block bonds to the part, clears every other module and leaves the holder room above the pad.

Ballast is gel: once the new arm is inside the new tail, the parent docks face to face and fills its circuits above the water line with gel through its line instead of air, as the head's lip circuit takes gel. The frame of the new arm is pinned into cast sockets printed into the new tail's floor, so the body holds the arm down. No steel in the new body.
The quilt starts just under the water line: below it the walls are the flat double skin of the floor, so no air under the water lifts the bodies, and the new tail rests on the floor when it is born.

The tile set is taken by the new tail itself, with the holder it took from the tray: Bergsonne style tiles (Core T44-14, Sense T44 motion and pressure, Power T48) and an mp6 pump on one cast tile, slid into a pocket of its own port flank.

text.birth: The new tail is printed whole, in one print, folded flat on the bowl floor (laid flat, Z folded 3 across and 3 along, 18 layers), around nothing: it is born empty, nose first. (a) The ball needle of the holder sits in the valve at the rim; the keel fills first and opens the lengthwise folds until the nose lies on the lip, paying the strip out from the front while the rim stays at the back of the pack (the tail is longer than the run from the face to the lip). (b) The holder and then its folding crank push the rim at 2 mm/s while the last folds open and air is fed with the advance, until the nose lies on the tank floor; each row opens across and then fills only once it lies outside, past the lip. (d) The needle leaves; the parent backs away on its wheels with its head, the front of the newborn resting on the floor, and the rest slides over the lip and settles.
text.solved: Solved by the script: the two skins of every body (built as the head is built), the folded pack, the path over the lip from the head's own skins, the reach of every pose with the DexArm's kinematics and joint ranges, the join poses of the new arm, the grip bosses, the heading of every part on the tray, the penetration of every pair in every frame. Interpolated: the shape of a row between flat, folded and filled during a birth (kinematic, as the head's birth), the settling of the rear of a newborn onto the floor, the drives of the tails (kinematic, no slip). Estimated: module masses, magnet pull on a pad, friction, gel drag, the base shroud.
text.handover: The parent's tail leaves its head at the port glass and goes round it. For each part it turns on the spot to the tray at the starboard glass, takes the part with its holder, drives to its stand beside the assembly plate at the new tail's face and sets the part down: base, pack, upper arm, forearm, end effector. The new arm, powered by its pack, holds each joint where the next module goes on. Whole, it folds and drives itself into the new tail. The parent docks face to face with the new tail and fills its circuits with gel ballast, then backs away. The new tail turns to the tray and takes a holder and a tile set itself.
